transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, what brought me in is... I keep hearing a man's voice. I work as a mechanic, and lately I hear this voice coming from the garage vents, and sometimes even from under the hood of the cars. 

It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. He just keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and he tells me not to touch certain cars. It's getting really hard to work and just... deal with things, so I needed to come in.
Do you find yourself believing the things the voice says about your husband, even when you try to tell yourself it might not be true?

Yes, I do. I mean, I know it probably sounds far-fetched, but... I'm still convinced that my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and the security cameras at work to track what I'm doing. 

They try to tell me I'm wrong, and they even show me the security footage and say, look, there's nothing there. But... I just still believe it anyway. I know they're tracking me.

Aside from hearing this voice and feeling watched, have you experienced any periods where your mood felt significantly different, such as feeling extremely low or unusually energetic and restless for days or weeks at a time?

Yeah, I do actually. Um... there are times where I just feel like I'm flying high. I get so much energy, it's like I can fix every single car in town by myself. 

But it doesn't stay a good feeling. I get really on edge. Like, if I'm in that mood and my husband asks why the dishes aren't done, or if one of the other techs just moves my socket set at the shop... I just blow up at them. I get so mad because it feels like they're trying to hold me down.
During those times when you feel that 'flying high' energy, do you hear the voice more often or more intensely than when you are feeling more like your usual self?

Yeah, I do. When I get into those moods... the times where I'm barely sleeping and just racing around the shop with all these big plans, I'm definitely still hearing the voice from the vents. And during all of that, I'm also still absolutely certain that the EV chargers and the cameras are being used to watch me. So, yeah, the voices and the feeling of being tracked are right there with me while I have all that energy.

According to DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria, if psychotic symptoms occur only during a mood episode, the diagnosis is mood disorder with psychotic features rather than schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia.
